newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo 1996 tourism down 6.6 pct vs 1995 - statistics.
newsitem.headline: Yugo 1996 tourism down 6.6 pct vs 1995 - statistics.

text.p: Yugoslavia registered around 2.85 million tourists in 1996, or 6.6 percent less than the previous year, the Federal Statistics Office reported on Wednesday.
Yugoslavs accounted for 2.55 million of the total, down 9.8 percent against 1995.
Visitors from other former Yugoslav republics -- Bosnia, Croatia, Macedonia and Slovenia -- rose 8.9 percent to 139,319.
The number of foreign visitors jumped by 62.8 percent to 162,109, with most, or 18,411, coming from the Russian Federation.
Tourists from Italy were next, with 17,840 registered visitors, followed by 13,135 from Greece, 12,534 from Bulgaria and 11,959 from Germany.

According to data available from the National Bank of Yugoslavia, hard currency income in the January-November 1996 period stood at $40.2 million, ar 7.8 percent more than in the same 11-month period in 1995.
NOTE -- Data is based on reception figures from hotels and other accommodation facilities. -- Amra Kevic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 2224305
